newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Belgium hints at visa-free entry for Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Belgium hints at visa-free entry for Hong Kong.

text.p: Belgian Foreign Minister Erik Derycke said on Thursday his country would attempt to grant visa-free entry to Hong Kong people after the British territory reverted to Chinese rule in June.

Derycke, in Singapore for a meeting of Asian and European foreign ministers, told reporters it would be difficult for Brussels to reach a decision on the issue before the handover at midnight on June 30.

"We would try to do everything that is convenient to have this adminstration work together with the UK people to ... negotiate a solution in favour of the people of Hong Kong," he told reporters upon his arrival at Changi Airport.
Asked if the decision could be reached before the handover, he said "it will be difficult".
Hong Kong, under British colonial rule for more than 150 years, will become a Special Administrative Region (SAR) after its return to China.
Top officials of the colony, including Governor Chris Patten and his deputies, have been lobbying hard for other countries to grant visa-free access to Hong Kong passports holders.
